subject: Order Form / MSA: Loss allocation — proposed examples and compromise
messages:
From: Jake Morales <jake@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement - Acme Corp <procurement@acme.com>, Legal - Acme Corp <legal@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ACME Order Form - liability carveouts

Evelyn —

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, our legal team has pushed back on the draft Order Form that removes carveouts for lost profits and loss of data. Attached is our redline to the Order Form (ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx). High level: Acme needs the ability to recover lost profits and data restoration costs where Redwood's acts or omissions cause a material outage or data loss, and we can't accept a blanket limitation to fees for those categories.

Questions for you: can Redwood accept a limited carveout for (i) direct loss of data (reasonable restoration costs plus forensics) and (ii) lost profits that are demonstrably caused by Redwood's gross negligence? If not, what alternative cap would you propose?

Jake
Procurement — Acme Corp

Attachment: ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (document stub)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Morales <jake@acme.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Legal - Acme Corp <legal@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME Order Form - liability carveouts

Jake —

Thanks for sending the redline and for the clarity on Acme's position. We want to be reasonable here while protecting our platform economics and liability exposure. Initial thoughts:

- We can consider a narrow data-restoration carveout tied to documented data loss caused by Redwood (not downstream third-party integrations), capped at the greater of (a) actual restoration costs and (b) 6 months of fees for the impacted product lines.
- For lost profits, Redwood's approach has been to limit indirect/consequential damages but allow direct loss recovery (e.g., invoiced revenue for the affected period). We are uncomfortable making gross negligence the trigger for lost profits carveout — that standard is hard to prove and creates open-ended exposure.

I'm looping in Markus (Legal) with suggested draft language and three short drafting examples to help bridge the gap. If we can agree on specific caps and a narrow list of carveouts, we can fold the language into the order form and move to DocuSign.

Best,
Evelyn
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jake Morales <jake@acme.com>, Legal - Acme Corp <legal@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME Order Form - liability carveouts (proposed draft clauses)

Team / Jake —

Below are three drafting examples intended to be constructive compromises. They try to: (1) preserve Redwood's overall cap approach, (2) allow a narrow, well-defined remedy for data loss and proven lost profits, and (3) avoid open-ended consequential exposure. Pick one and we can convert it into a redline.

Example A (narrow restoration carveout + fees cap):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, special, incidental or punitive damages, including lost profits, except that Customer may recover (i) direct costs of data restoration reasonably incurred to restore Customer Data to the state immediately prior to the event ("Data Restoration Costs") and (ii) direct documented lost revenue demonstrably caused by a Redwood outage resulting in loss of access to the Service for a period exceeding 24 continuous hours ("Lost Revenue"). With respect to clauses (i) and (ii), Redwood's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (A) the fees paid by Customer under the Order Form in the 12 months preceding the event and (B) $500,000."

Rationale: keeps carveouts focused on measurable economic losses, uses objective triggers (24-hour outage), and sets a definite cap.

Example B (tiered cap + enhanced SLA remedy):
"Subject to the limitation of liability, for breaches involving Customer Data loss or confirmed data corruption caused by Redwood, Redwood will (i) provide commercially reasonable assistance to restore data, (ii) reimburse documented restoration costs up to the lesser of $250,000 or six months' fees, and (iii) if the outage meets the criteria in Exhibit A (Critical SLA Failure), Customer may recover direct lost profits proven with reasonable documentation up to 12 months' fees. For avoidance of doubt, consequential damages remain excluded except for the foregoing."

Rationale: ties recovery to SLA failures and gives a path for higher recovery if strict SLA failure criteria are met (helps operations and remediate incentives).

Example C (cap carveout with indemnity for data breaches):
"Except as set forth below, consequential damages are excluded. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood shall be liable for (i) Data Restoration Costs and (ii) reasonable and documented lost profits to the extent caused by Redwood's willful misconduct or material breach of its obligations concerning Customer Data, in each case subject to an aggregate cap equal to the greater of six months' fees or $1,000,000. For incidents involving unauthorized access to Customer Data, Redwood shall also trigger the mutual incident response procedures set out in Exhibit B."

Rationale: preserves higher remedy only for willful misconduct/material breach and ties to incident response and forensic standards to limit speculative claims.

Practical negotiation note: Acme appears focused on lost profits and restoration — propose we offer Example B as a middle ground (SLA-based pathway to recover lost profits) and give specific SLA criteria in Exhibit A so there is an objective test. Monica — can you draft the Exhibit A SLA thresholds (downtime, severity, measurement) and the forensic/restore steps for Exhibit B?

-Markus
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: msa_proposed_clauses_patch.txt (contains the three examples above as redline-ready snippets)

From: Legal - Acme Corp <legal@acme.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Jake Morales <jake@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME Order Form - liability carveouts (counter)

Markus / Evelyn —

Thanks for the suggested language. Acme appreciates the effort to set objective triggers, but our position remains that lost profits caused by Redwood's negligence (not just willful misconduct) should be recoverable in cases where Redwood's failure is the proximate cause. We cannot accept a position that requires a 24-hour outage threshold for all lost profits — some business-critical endpoints incur outsized loss on shorter interruptions.

Counter-proposal: we will accept an SLA-based pathway for certain services (per Example B), provided that: (1) SLA metrics for high-impact endpoints are set with shorter thresholds (e.g., 2 hours for transactional write endpoints), and (2) the data restoration carveout explicitly covers forensic costs plus reasonable remediation. We can live with a monetary cap of 12 months' fees but would like the ability to seek lost profits within that cap for negligence-based incidents.

We will upload a short redline with the narrow changes to your Example B language. If Redwood can accept the SLA adjustments and the 12-month cap for proven lost profits, Acme can move to sign within the week.

— Acme Legal
Attachment: none

Subject: Re: ACME Order Form - liability carveouts (next steps)

Thanks all — good progress. Quick plan:

1) Monica will produce Exhibit A (SLA thresholds) with a split for "Core transactional endpoints" (2-hour failure threshold) and "Batch/reporting endpoints" (24-hour threshold) by EOD tomorrow; Monica, please attach to this thread when ready.
2) Markus will incorporate the forensic-cost language and set the monetary cap to 12 months' fees for the agreed carveouts.
3) Jake / Acme Legal to provide the final redline to Example B once Monica's Exhibit A is attached.

If we can close those three items, commercial can push to DocuSign and we will accept the 12-month cap as the compromise.

Evelyn
